source_text: Quid ergo etiam haec disputatio collegerit, prudens lector attendat. Apostolus dixit in plures abundasse donationem Christi ad salutem, quam Adae culpa nocuisset.
pass_a_gloss: What therefore even this disputation has collected, let the prudent reader attend. The Apostle said that the donation of Christ abounded unto more toward salvation than Adam's fault had harmed.
pass_b_english: Let the discerning reader consider what this further argument has established. The apostle said that Christ’s gift abounded to the salvation of more people than Adam’s fault had harmed (Romans 5:15).

choices.why: Julian's pair with iustitia: guilt as culpable will, not a nature.
Paul in Julian's citations; keep Apostle not 'Paul' unless Paulus is written.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

bible_refs.note: From Pass B Scripture tagging; wording follows Julian's Latin, not a modern Bible.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
